executive_summary: Complete the writer half of payload.urgency='interrupt': add a validated, discoverable stamp path at the shared dispatch chokepoint, fix a stale doc pointer, and close the reader/writer shape gap QF-20260912-269's merged reader left open.

functional_requirements.requirement: Add a shared urgency-levels constant and a validated urgency pass-through in lib/coordinator/dispatch.cjs's insertCoordinationRow/dispatchToWorker so a caller can mark payload.urgency='interrupt' through a named, discoverable option instead of ad hoc payload construction.
functional_requirements.description: VALIDATION (sub_agent_execution_results 39101e4d) confirmed 0 of 1755 live session_coordination rows carry payload.urgency NOT NULL because no writer exists anywhere in scripts/ or lib/ (excl. archive/). Explore (705eca19) located the shared chokepoint at lib/coordinator/dispatch.cjs:1453 (insertCoordinationRow) and :1905 (dispatchToWorker), and the structural precedent this fix was modeled on: lib/sd/amend-sd.js:291-310's fence_notice payload construction. Add a new lib/coordinator/urgency-levels.cjs exporting URGENCY_LEVELS = ['interrupt'] plus an isKnownUrgency(value) helper, and thread an optional opts.urgency through dispatchToWorker/insertCoordinationRow that sets row.payload.urgency when provided (a caller may also set payload.urgency directly, since payload is unrestricted JSONB — this FR makes the path named and validated, not newly possible).
acceptance_criteria: dispatchToWorker(supabase, row, { urgency: 'interrupt' }) results in a persisted row whose payload.urgency === 'interrupt'
Calling dispatchToWorker/insertCoordinationRow with no urgency option produces a row byte-identical to pre-change behavior (no new required fields, no default injected)

An unrecognized urgency value (not in URGENCY_LEVELS) is still passed through unmodified onto payload.urgency and logs one warning line via the existing logger convention, matching coordination-inbox.cjs's own fail-open style for its urgentRows fetch

functional_requirements.requirement: Fix the stale documentation pointer at scripts/hooks/coordination-inbox.cjs:842-843 and add a real 'Urgency escalation (payload.urgency)' subsection to docs/protocol/coordinator-adam-comms.md that cross-references the full spec already written at docs/reference/fleet-coordination.md:173-194.
functional_requirements.description: The in-code comment claims the urgency class is 'documented in docs/protocol/coordinator-adam-comms.md beside fence_notice', but that file has zero occurrences of 'urgency' or 'fence_notice' (VALIDATION 39101e4d, corroborated independently by Explore 705eca19). The real section lives only in docs/reference/fleet-coordination.md:173-194. Explore identified two candidate insertion points in coordinator-adam-comms.md: the 'Receipt contract — ALL directive kinds' section (lines 115-162) and the 'Optional, validated typed --kind at send' section (lines 368-393). Insert a short subsection near the Receipt contract section (the natural home, since it already covers how directive-kind rows are received) that names payload.urgency='interrupt', the new dispatchToWorker({ urgency: 'interrupt' }) option from FR-1, and links to fleet-coordination.md for the full reader-side behavior. Update the coordination-inbox.cjs comment to name the correct file.
acceptance_criteria: grep -c 'urgency' docs/protocol/coordinator-adam-comms.md returns >= 1 after this SD ships
The code comment at scripts/hooks/coordination-inbox.cjs (formerly lines 842-843) names a file that actually contains the word 'urgency'
The new subsection cross-references docs/reference/fleet-coordination.md rather than duplicating its content verbatim

functional_requirements.requirement: Add a test proving the writer (FR-1) and the already-merged reader (coordination-inbox.cjs's mergePriorityExempt / classifyToolActiveLaneBlind) agree on payload shape end-to-end, closing the 'readers-without-writer' / zero-yield-by-construction gap VALIDATION flagged as its sole HIGH finding.
functional_requirements.description: The 4 existing reader-side tests (tests/unit/coordination-inbox-priority-exempt.test.js, tests/unit/coordination-inbox-lane-blind-nudge.test.js) are pure-function tests fed a hand-built urgentRows array; none exercises a row actually produced by the writer. Add a unit test that builds a row via the FR-1 dispatchToWorker urgency option (with a stubbed Supabase client, no live DB call) and feeds its resulting payload into the existing pure reader functions, asserting it is recognized as an urgent row.
acceptance_criteria: A new test constructs a row through the FR-1 writer path (not a hand-typed literal) and asserts classifyToolActiveLaneBlind(row, { cutMinutes: 2 }).blind === true when the row is old enough
The same test asserts mergePriorityExempt correctly places a writer-produced urgent row ahead of the oldest-five batch
The test requires no live Supabase connection (stubbed/mocked client only), consistent with this repo's DB-tier integration constraint

functional_requirements.requirement: Preserve and document, without modification, the already-merged reader-side mechanism delivered by QF-20260912-269 (PR #8889): the uncapped urgentRows fetch, the red URGENT label, and the cutMinutes:2 lane-blind nudge in scripts/hooks/coordination-inbox.cjs.
functional_requirements.description: VALIDATION confirmed all four target files (scripts/hooks/coordination-inbox.cjs, the two new test files, docs/reference/fleet-coordination.md) are byte-identical to origin/main and that `npx vitest run` on the two test files reports 2 files / 41 tests passed. This FR carries no new code; it exists so this PRD's acceptance criteria and EXEC-phase regression checks explicitly assert against the delivered baseline rather than silently assuming it.
acceptance_criteria: scripts/hooks/coordination-inbox.cjs, tests/unit/coordination-inbox-priority-exempt.test.js, tests/unit/coordination-inbox-lane-blind-nudge.test.js, and docs/reference/fleet-coordination.md remain byte-identical to origin/main except for the FR-2 comment-pointer fix
`npx vitest run tests/unit/coordination-inbox-priority-exempt.test.js tests/unit/coordination-inbox-lane-blind-nudge.test.js` continues to report 0 failures after this SD's changes land

functional_requirements.requirement: Explicitly disposition the SD's optional fix-shape limb (e) — a UserPromptSubmit read of interrupt rows — as DEFERRED for this SD rather than letting it lapse silently.
functional_requirements.description: The originating ticket marked limb (e) 'optional, measured at PLAN'. PLAN's disposition: DEFERRED. coordination-inbox.cjs's existing PostToolUse poll (CHECK_INTERVAL_MS = 15 seconds) already surfaces an interrupt row within one cycle for any tool-active session; a second UserPromptSubmit hook path would be redundant without a demonstrated gap (e.g., a session quiet on tool calls long enough that no PostToolUse fires between an interrupt row landing and the next prompt). No code is added for this FR.
acceptance_criteria: The SD record and this PRD explicitly state limb (e) is deferred, with the reason recorded, rather than being silently dropped
If a future incident demonstrates a real gap, it is filed as a new, separately-scoped QF/SD rather than reopening this one

technical_requirements.requirement: The urgency validation/pass-through in dispatch.cjs must fail-open: an unrecognized value is logged and still written, never thrown, and never blocks the insert.
technical_requirements.rationale: dispatch.cjs's insertCoordinationRow is the single chokepoint for every coordinator send across the fleet (fleet-dashboard.cjs, capped-pool-broadcast.cjs, amend-sd.js). A throwing validation here has fleet-wide blast radius; the existing urgentRows reader fetch in coordination-inbox.cjs already uses a try/catch fail-open pattern for the same reason, so this change matches established convention.

technical_requirements.requirement: The recognized urgency values must live in one shared, importable constant (lib/coordinator/urgency-levels.cjs), not be re-typed as a string literal at each call site.
technical_requirements.rationale: The existing topic field is free-form and has already drifted (coordinator-capacity-forecast.mjs uses topic:'source_work', this SD's ticket uses topic:'ruling', with no shared enum). A single exported constant prevents the same drift from recurring for urgency and gives FR-2's documentation and FR-3's tests one source of truth to reference.

technical_requirements.requirement: No new database column or migration. payload.urgency continues to live inside the existing session_coordination.payload JSONB column.
technical_requirements.rationale: The reader side (already merged) reads payload->>urgency directly with no schema change; the writer side must not introduce asymmetry by requiring a migration the reader never needed. Confirmed session_coordination's live schema already supports arbitrary JSONB keys with no CHECK constraint on payload shape.

system_architecture.overview: This SD completes the writer half of the payload.urgency='interrupt' mechanism whose reader half (scripts/hooks/coordination-inbox.cjs) already merged via QF-20260912-269/PR#8889. It adds a named, validated way for a coordinator-authored ruling to set payload.urgency at the existing dispatch chokepoint (lib/coordinator/dispatch.cjs), and repairs a stale documentation cross-reference discovered during LEAD-TO-PLAN validation.

components.name: urgency-levels constant
components.responsibility: Single source of truth for recognized urgency values ('interrupt' initially); consumed by the writer for validation/warning and referenced by tests and documentation.

components.name: dispatch.cjs writer extension
components.responsibility: Accept an optional urgency signal at the insertCoordinationRow/dispatchToWorker chokepoint, validate it against the shared constant (fail-open on unrecognized values), and ensure it lands in the persisted payload.urgency.

components.name: coordinator-adam-comms.md documentation
components.responsibility: Discoverable, accurate authoring-time reference telling a coordinator session how to mark a ruling as interrupt-worthy, cross-referencing the full reader-side spec.

system_architecture.data_flow: A coordinator session decides a ruling reverses in-flight work, then calls dispatchToWorker(supabase, row, { urgency: 'interrupt' }) (FR-1). The row lands in session_coordination with payload.urgency='interrupt'. The already-merged reader in coordination-inbox.cjs fetches urgentRows uncapped (gated on payload->>urgency='interrupt'), merges them ahead of the oldest-five batch via mergePriorityExempt, prints a red URGENT label, and the lane-blind nudge fires at cutMinutes:2 naming the row's subject.
integration_points: scripts/hooks/coordination-inbox.cjs (already-merged reader, unmodified except the FR-2 comment fix)

test_scenarios.then: The row object passed to supabase.from('session_coordination').insert(...) has payload.urgency === 'interrupt'

test_scenarios.then: The inserted row's payload has no urgency key added, and every other field matches the pre-FR-1 output exactly (regression pin)

test_scenarios.then: No exception is thrown, payload.urgency === 'not-a-real-level' on the inserted row, and exactly one warning is logged via the existing logger convention

test_scenarios.scenario: The shared urgency-levels constant correctly classifies known and unknown values
test_scenarios.then: Returns true only for 'interrupt'; false for 'bogus', null, and '' — no exception for any input type

test_scenarios.scenario: A row produced by the FR-1 writer path is correctly recognized by the already-merged reader's pure functions

acceptance_criteria: Calling dispatchToWorker(supabase, row, { urgency: 'interrupt' }) results in a row whose payload.urgency === 'interrupt', verified by TS-1

Every pre-existing caller of dispatchToWorker/insertCoordinationRow (fleet-dashboard.cjs, capped-pool-broadcast.cjs, lib/sd/amend-sd.js) continues to produce byte-identical rows with zero regressions in their existing test suites

docs/protocol/coordinator-adam-comms.md contains a real 'Urgency escalation' subsection (grep -c 'urgency' >= 1) and the coordination-inbox.cjs code comment names a file that actually documents the mechanism
TS-5's integration-shaped unit test demonstrates the writer (FR-1) and the already-merged reader agree on payload shape, closing VALIDATION's HIGH finding without requiring a live production ruling
`npx vitest run` across the coordination-inbox.cjs and dispatch.cjs test files reports 0 failures, including the 41 pre-existing tests VALIDATION confirmed passing plus all TS-1 through TS-5

risks.risk: A future caller sets payload.urgency to a plausible-but-wrong string (e.g. 'urgent' instead of 'interrupt') and is silently ignored by the reader, recreating the same consumer-without-matching-writer gap in a new shape.
risks.mitigation: The shared urgency-levels constant (TR-2) plus a mandatory warning log (FR-1's TS-3) surfaces any unrecognized value at write time rather than leaving it silently unread.
risks.rollback_plan: No data-destructive rollback needed: unrecognized values are passed through, never dropped, so a future fix to the constant (adding the correct value) makes historical rows retroactively meaningful with no backfill.

risks.risk: Adding validation/logging to the hot dispatchToWorker/insertCoordinationRow chokepoint (used by every coordinator send path across the fleet) regresses an unrelated caller.
risks.mitigation: The change is purely additive (a new optional opts.urgency parameter); it never executes unless the field is present, and TS-2 pins byte-identical output for every caller that omits it.
risks.rollback_plan: Revert the isolated diff to lib/coordinator/dispatch.cjs and lib/coordinator/urgency-levels.cjs (~15-20 LOC total); no other file's runtime behavior depends on this change.

risks.risk: The FR-2 doc-pointer fix is misread by a future auditor as evidence the reader implementation itself changed, when only a comment and a doc file moved.
risks.mitigation: Keep the FR-2 diff isolated to the comment string and the markdown file; call out explicitly in the PR description and in FR-4's acceptance criteria that coordination-inbox.cjs's functional code is unchanged.
risks.rollback_plan: Revert the single-line comment edit and the markdown addition; no functional code is touched.

phases.description: Add lib/coordinator/urgency-levels.cjs and wire the optional urgency option through insertCoordinationRow/dispatchToWorker in lib/coordinator/dispatch.cjs.
Fix the stale pointer in scripts/hooks/coordination-inbox.cjs and add the real cross-referencing subsection to docs/protocol/coordinator-adam-comms.md.
Add the integration-shaped unit test proving the writer and the already-merged reader agree, then run the full relevant test suite to confirm zero regressions.
deliverables: Full vitest run evidence (coordination-inbox.cjs + dispatch.cjs test files)

technical_decisions: Reuse the existing dispatchToWorker/insertCoordinationRow chokepoint rather than building a new CLI: Explore's research (705eca19) found no single dedicated 'ruling' CLI exists today — the one historical topic='ruling' row was ad hoc, not from a purpose-built helper — so any future caller (script or ad hoc) benefits from validation living at the shared chokepoint rather than in a new, single-purpose tool.

Do not attempt automatic detection of 'reverses in-flight work': Explore confirmed no existing classifier fits (payload.message_kind's CORRECTION_KINDS is about correcting prior messages, not build-direction reversal) and building a new one is disproportionate risk/scope for this fix. The caller (coordinator judgment) supplies the flag explicitly, matching the originating ticket's own text: 'the coordinator decides at authoring time.'

patterns_identified: The reader-side fail-open try/catch pattern for optional/uncapped fetches (urgentRows, priorityRows) should be mirrored on the writer side for validation warnings.

fence_notice is the only pre-existing precedent for a payload discriminator with both a real writer (lib/sd/amend-sd.js) and a real reader (coordination-inbox.cjs's PRIORITY_EXEMPT_DIRECTIVE_KINDS) — the new urgency mechanism should reach the same writer+reader completeness.
Free-form string fields (topic, message_kind) drift without a shared enum; urgency should not repeat that mistake.
key_decisions: Scope this SD to the writer + docs + shape-agreement test only, since the reader is already merged and verified (QF-20260912-269/PR#8889) — re-touching the reader risks an unnecessary regression on 41 passing tests.
Defer fix-shape limb (e) (UserPromptSubmit read) explicitly rather than implement or silently drop it, per FR-5.
